meta.title: Shenzhou-20 reentry
meta.mission: Uncrewed return of the Shenzhou-20 spacecraft (cracked window) from the China Space Station to the Dongfeng landing site, 19 January 2026.

orbit.tle_epoch: Space-Track gp_history for NORAD 63632 (SZ-20); epoch 2026-01-19 00:56:12 UTC, the last element set consistent with the pre-burn orbit (mean motion follows the decay trend of the previous sets; the 17:50 UTC set is a post-landing propagation artefact).

notes: Reconstruction, not official ephemeris: a 3-DOF simulation (WGS-84, J2, rotating Earth, NRLMSIS 2.1 column) of the deorbit burn, return-module entry with Mach-dependent capsule drag and 0.30 L/D bank steering, and the parachute sequence, solved so that the capsule reaches the reported landing point and minute for a deorbit ignition set by the reported orbital-module separation minute.

The orbit before the burn is SGP4 from the spacecraft's own Space-Track element set; the Earth-fixed track does not change with the T0 slider, which only moves the Sun (for exploring the illumination of a return at another time of day).
Plasma blackout is marked between the published 80 km and 40 km heights; the orange glow is an illustration of the self-luminous trail, not a brightness model.
Winds, the retro-rocket pulse, attitude dynamics and the real guidance law are not modeled; the single bank reversal is a proxy for the roll-modulated entry guidance.
